#6713. I'm a Mom of Two, and This Ernesta Rug Gives Me That Luxe Look With the Easy Cleanup of a Washable Option

Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

I have to admit, I have a bit of a gripe with washable rugs. For years, the design industry has been trying to convince us that the answer to a beautiful, livable home is a washable rug. And while I understand the appeal, especially as a mom to two young kids, a dog, and a household that sees its fair share of spills, muddy shoes, and general chaos, I’ve just never been entirely sold on the idea.

While washable rug options have definitely improved over the years, there’s still something about the weight, texture, and character of a traditional rug that I find hard to forgo for the sake of washability. I want a rug that feels substantial underfoot, looks better with age, and doesn’t require me to wrestle an eight-by-ten-foot piece of fabric into my washing machine every time someone spills a juice box.

When I learned about Ernesta’s protective rug treatment, I was intrigued. The custom rug brand offers an optional treatment designed to help repel spills and make everyday messes easier to clean, without requiring you to compromise on your rug’s style, material, or size. In theory, it offers the best of both worlds: the look and feel of a beautifully made rug, with a little extra insurance against the realities of family life. Plus, it’s a treatment that’s typically hard to access on your own without going custom through a designer.

I actually have several Ernesta rugs in my home (I’m a huge fan of their quality and approachable customization options!), but after swapping in an Ernesta rug treated with the brand’s protective finish in our living room, I don’t think I’ll ever go back to ordering a rug without it. Here’s what you should know about the treatment, how it's held up in my own home, and why I think it may be a smarter investment than yet another washable rug.

Best for: This rug is an excellent option for families, pet owners, or anyone who just prefers not to have to be too precious with their things.

Not ideal for: Anyone looking for a quick-ship rug option.

Bottom Line: The customization of Ernesta’s rug assortment makes it easy to get the exact look and function that serves your home best, including different sizes, non-slip bases, and protections.

One of the reasons I love Ernesta so much is how approachable they make the ordering process. There’s no visiting a showroom or making 400 phone calls to try to get the right custom-cut size. You simply log on to their site, browse the options, then choose up to five samples to try for just $10.

My samples came incredibly quickly—within a few days, they were at my doorstep, ready for review. Because I already liked the look of the rug we had in our living room (more on that later), I knew I didn’t want to stray too far from the neutral, functional foundation it gave us.

When we started, we had Ernesta’s Emerson sisal rug in the space. The nubby texture and color looked beautiful, but it was a bit small (it was originally sized to an old home that we have since moved from), and the deeper grooves of the weave made it hard to clean up spills. I have two young kids and a dog, and truly not a day goes by where someone hasn’t spilled yogurt or cracker crumbs or juice on the rug.

Still, I don’t think you should have to sacrifice beauty for function in a family home, and Ernesta helped us find that balance. After debating between a few different styles, I ended up settling on the Cally wool flatweave rug in Camel. Wool flatweave rugs are notoriously durable on their own, and I knew the protective coating would only help it hold up better. Bonus: The tighter weave meant fewer nooks and crannies for gunk to get into.

Once we decided on our new style, we measured out the size we’d need, which ended up being around 13 x 15 feet. I loved how easy it was to order the exact size we needed for our space, especially given that it wasn’t a standard measurement. If you’re unsure about the right size for your rug (or how many legs of your furniture should be on the rug at one time), Ernesta has helpful guidance on their site.

Placing the order was easy; you can opt into the protective treatment before adding the order to your cart, as well as choose other details, like the type of edge binding and whether you’d like to include a rug pad (we chose the attached version).

Protective treatments for rugs are nothing new; they’ve been available to design industry insiders for years. That said, very few DTC companies offer the treatment, unless you’re buying through a designer or want to seek out a supplier on your own.

That’s what’s so great about Ernesta’s offerings—it’s literally as easy as checking a box before you add your rug to cart. The treatment starts at $62 and increases depending on the size of your rug. Their formula is non-toxic and works by acting as a protective layer between the surface of the rug and any spills or debris, preventing stains from setting in and keeping the fibers intact for longer.

Receiving and installing our Ernesta rug couldn’t have been easier, especially considering its large size. It was delivered and placed in our entryway, where it waited for a few days until my husband and I had a spare moment to lay it out.

The rug was packaged beautifully, with thick plastic wrapping protecting the roll, a firm cardboard tube at the center, and fabric wrapping the edges so the binding didn’t get roughed up in transit. I thought this was a particularly nice touch.

As with most rugs, the corners were a bit flared when we first unrolled it, so here’s my favorite tip: add several ice cubes to any corner you want to lay flat and let them melt. The slow dissipation of moisture will relax the rug's fibers, and by the time it has melted away completely, you should have a totally flat rug.

I was immediately impressed by the look and feel of this rug—the wool was so soft and plush, and the rubber mat integrated on the bottom meant it did not budge once we laid it down (though it did make it difficult to reposition when we laid it a little wonky initially, word to the wise). There was no “chemical” smell from the protective treatments, and the fibers still felt just as soft as they did on the sample I received before ordering.

Aesthetically, I love the vibe that this rug brings to the space. It’s soft and plush and cozy, and finally in better proportion with the rest of the room—which is great, because I have a pair of armchairs I won at auction waiting in the wings for their moment. Before, they were floating off the rug and looked odd, but now, they’ll be perfect.

Logically, the protective treatment was 100 percent the right choice for our family. Not even five minutes after laying it out, my three-year-old squished an applesauce pouch on the rug, and it came up with ease. In the month since having it, we’ve definitely put this rug through the paces of family life, and it still looks as good as the day we opened it. Cleaning it is easy, and Ernesta has a whole page on their site dedicated to care instructions, depending on the material your rug is made of.

Overall, this is the ideal solution to me: a rug that looks as good as it performs, and doesn’t require any design sacrifice (or yelling from mom) in the process.

#6710. These Expert-Loved Ceramide Moisturizers Will Save Your Skin Barrier

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

These formulas are basically a cheat code to supple, hydrated, healthy skin.

If you shop as much as ELLE’s beauty-obsessed editors, you’re already pretty familiar with a few common skin care ingredients. Those with acne-prone skin know the benefits of salicylic acid, retinol, and mandelic acid all too well. Oily skin types typically reach for non-comedogenic formulas, while dry skin drinks up hyaluronic acid. Still, if there’s one ingredient all skin types can use in a routine, it’s ceramides. New to that world? Let us help you get more familiar.

“Ceramides are fats, or lipids, that your skin makes on its own,” explains Dr. Anne Han. While you might not have heard of them, think of ceramides as your skin’s security guard. “They make up about half of the lipids in the stratum corneum, the outermost layer of skin. I like the ‘brick and mortar’ picture: skin cells are the bricks, and ceramides, along with cholesterol and fatty acids, are the mortar that holds them together. That mortar keeps water in and keeps irritants, allergens, and microbes out,” she adds. When your skin becomes particularly dry and crackly, this could be a sign that it needs a ceramide boost.

“When ceramide levels drop, the barrier gets ‘leaky.’ Water evaporates more easily, and skin turns dry, tight, flaky, itchy, and more reactive. That happens with eczema, as we age, in cold, dry weather, and with overwashing or harsh actives. Ceramides in a moisturizer help top up what the skin is missing,” Dr. Han shares. Not all skin care products offer instant gratification, but adding a ceramide moisturizer to your lineup can boost moisture levels “sometimes within a day of the first use, with more benefit after a few weeks of steady use,” Dr. Han suggests, adding that “studies show ceramide moisturizers raise skin hydration and cut water loss” and “work best alongside cholesterol and fatty acids, the other two parts of the skin’s natural lipid mix, not on their own.”

All in all, every skin type can benefit from a ceramide moisturizer for an instant boost of moisture and overall improvement in skin over time. If your skin is in need of a tune-up, the list below, featuring derm- and ELLE editor-approved picks, is the perfect place to start. Shop every type of formula, from K-beauty staples to splurge-worthy finds.

This fan-favorite CeraVe cream has reached cult status for good reason. As with most formulas from the brand, this moisturizing tub is packed with ceramides and hyaluronic acid, which lock in and attract moisture, respectively.

Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, ceramides

Expert review: “[This has] several skin-identical ceramides with glycerin, is fragrance-free, works for face and body, and is affordable.”—Dr. Anne Han, MD

The powerhouse trio in this formula plays key roles in restoring and balancing the skin: ceramides protect, niacinamide addresses discoloration, and glycerin provides moisture. Together, they leave your skin deeply nourished and supple. Take it a step further with the SPF 30 version for even more protection.

Key ingredients: Prebiotic thermal water, ceramides, niacinamide, glycerin

Expert review: “It contains ceramides plus niacinamide, which can calm redness.”—Dr. Han

While a hydrated, moisturized barrier can improve the look of fine lines and wrinkles, this SkinCeuticals formula is designed to deliver a healthy moisture boost. With vitamin E, lipids, essential oils, and more, skin becomes smoother, suppler, and plumper with every use.

Key ingredients: Ceramides, vitamin E, essential oils

Expert review: “This has the full barrier-lipid trio, which is helpful for aging skin that recovers more slowly.”—AH

Packed with everything we love about K-beauty formulas—lightweight, hydrating, soothing—this barrier cream seeps into the skin like butter, improving its elasticity and suppleness.

Key ingredients: Ceramides, fatty acids, and cholesterol

ELLE editor review: “Believe it or not, my foray into Korean skin care came through Aestura’s products. In the dead of winter, when my semi-oily, acne-prone skin needed reprieve, I received a gift set with the brand’s bestsellers and instantly fell for this cream. My skin felt so hydrated and conditioned, and it even helped my makeup look more glowy (not greasy).”—Nerisha Penrose, beauty commerce editor

You’ve likely seen a TikTok video of someone applying this milky solution to their skin during a skin care routine or makeup tutorial. The barrier-strengthening “glazing milk” gives you an instant glow while working overtime to soothe and quench parched skin.

Customer review: “Oh how I love this essence. I usually use a thinner/clear essence but I am now a fan of this milky one. It gives an instant boost of hydration and helps with serum absorption.”

Medik8’s formulas are as straightforward as they come, with ceramides showing up in this moisturizer and its nighttime counterpart. In this composition, the main ingredient is combined with hyaluronic acid and peptides to protect stressed skin and visibly plump stressed skin over time.

Key ingredients: Ceramides, prebiotic peptides, hyaluronic acid

Customer review: “My skin feels great when I use it. Light enough for my oily skin but truly moisturizing, unlike others I’ve tried over the years which were either too light or too heavy.”

As the name suggests, the results are, in fact, instant. Think of this moisturizer as youthfulness in a bottle; it’s packed with moisturizing glycerin and urea, plus squalane, peptides, and ceramides for firming.

Key ingredients: Peptide blend (Dipalmityl hydroxylproline and hexapeptide-12), squalane, ceramides, glycerin, urea, and hyaluronic acid

ELLE editor review: “Look into my travel toiletry bag, and you’ll find about two of these tubes rolled down to their last squeeze—that’s just how much I love this cream. My skin feels instantly moisturized and supple, but looks even better when I wake up.”—NP

There’s power in numbers, so when shopping for an effective ceramide moisturizer, Dr. Han advises looking for one that combines similar ingredients. “Look for ceramides together with cholesterol and fatty acids, which mimic the skin’s own lipid mix. Ceramides used alone are less effective at barrier repair,” she says. Plus, look for formulas with “skin-identical” ceramides, which look like “ceramide NP, AP, or EOP (older names include ceramide 1, 3, and 6-II)” on labels.

Furthermore, you’ll want a moisturizer packed with “humectants, like glycerin or hyaluronic acid [which] pull water in” or “occlusives, like petrolatum or dimethicone to seal [moisture] in; niacinamide can help skin make more ofits own ceramides,” Dr. Han adds. Other important markers to look for include “fragrance-free” to avoid irritating sensitive or eczema-prone skin; for acne-prone skin, “non-comedogenic” products are great because they don’t clog pores.

“They do different jobs, so it isn’t really either/or. Ceramides are barrier ingredients and help the skin hold water and resist irritation, and that is what makes something a moisturizer,” Dr. Han explains. Meanwhile, peptides—skin care’s buzziest ingredient—are touted for their anti-aging properties. “They are meant to signal the skin to make more collagen or to soften the look of fine lines. If your main concern is dryness, sensitivity, redness, or eczema-prone skin, start with ceramides. The science behind them is more direct, since you are replacing a lipid your barrier actually lacks. If your barrier is in good shape and you want something for fine lines, a peptide product is a reasonable, gentle add-on,” she adds.

#6706. Dakota Johnson Wore Cherry Cola Nails, So Now I’m Wearing Cherry Cola Nails

A syrupy upgrade to your typical burgundy mani.

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

One of my guilty pleasures is sipping on a large vanilla cherry Coke at the movie theater. I’m really not a big soda drinker, but there’s just something about the combination of a fizzy, cherry-flavored soda, a bucket of popcorn, and a good movie that does it for me. And luckily for me, I’ve recently discovered another way to indulge: cherry cola nails. Yep, my go-to concession stand order is officially making its way to my fingertips, and naturally, I’m eating (or should I say drinking?) it up.

Dakota Johnson was also spotted wearing cherry cola nails earlier this month at a screening of Flesh Impact in Los Angeles, which only further fueled my need to get the look. Similar to syrup nails, these have a glossy finish to them, but are dark, rich, and reddish-brown, just like the classic soda. It’s basically the perfect marriage of two of my favorite fall nail colors, burgundy and chocolate brown. Ahead, everything you need to know about the trend, plus plenty of inspiration for your next nail appointment. Movie theater soda optional... but highly encouraged.

Think of a Cherry Coke: It’s dark brown with touches of red when the light hits just right. And that’s exactly the goal of the manicure version. “Cherry cola nails are the perfect blend of deep burgundy, rich chocolate brown, and a hint of red,” says celebrity nail artist Jacqueline Pham. “Think of that beautiful, dark cherry soda color that looks almost brown in certain lighting but has a cherry red undertone when the light hits.”

They’re also a great way to dress up your nails for the holiday season: “It’s a little sultry, and a fun alternative to your classic burgundy red manicure,” adds Pham. “You can play around with different shades of brown and burgundy and a slight change in either color can create a completely different cherry cola effect.”

Need some ideas of how exactly to incorporate the color onto your fingertips? Firstly, Pham suggests wearing them as a single-color mani—glossy and straightforward with a classic, high shine finish. “It’s timeless, elegant, and looks beautiful on both short and long nails,” she says. She also likes adding a little shimmer too, which you can do with the help of Essie’s Gel Couture Liquid Diamonds in Size Me Up or Color Street’s Nail Strips in Velvet Dahlia. If you’re craving some nail art, you could also do a twist on a classic French manicure with cherry cola tips over a sheer nude base.

First things first, you’ll want to reach for more than one bottle of nail polish. “The secret to achieving the perfect cherry cola shade is layering your colors rather than using just one,” says Pham. “I personally recommend starting with a rich chocolate brown as your first coat, followed by a deep burgundy as your second coat.” This mimics a cherry soda too, with a brown base and a hint of cherry flavor and color. “The brown creates a warm base, while the burgundy adds cherry tint,” explains Pham. After applying a base coat, she says to do “one thin coat of chocolate brown and one thin coat of burgundy, allowing each layer to dry.” After those two coats, she says to “finish with a high gloss top coat to give it that glassy, soda-like shine.”

Catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo. She’s covered and tested all things nails, from the coolest new polish colors to cuticle care and nail art trends.

#6704. The 25 Best Cocktails for Thanksgiving

With a whiskey warmer, spiced sour, or comforting classic in your hand, you can get through any awkward family gathering.

Are you ready for your annual awkward family gathering? Thanksgiving is finally here, and if thinking about safe topics to discuss with all three generations of your family is making you break out in hives, then rest assured we’ve got some recipes to give you the liquid courage to face it.

You’ve got the turkey basted and roasting in the oven. You’ve got your grandmother’s perfect mac and cheese. You’ve got mashed potatoes—the best. And you’ve got store-bought pie from your slacker cousin. But, wait, do you know what you’ll be drinking for the most important feast of the year? We promise: There’s something for everyone at your dinner table on this curated list of cocktails.

Does Grandpa only abide by the saying, “If it’s brown, drink it down?” We’ve got a few whiskey drinks that will keep him on ice. Did your aunt who drinks only French reds run through the bottle she brought already? There’s a sangria recipe that’ll have her too busy sipping to snip. Need a warm cup of something strong while you “take the dog for a walk”? There’s an Irish coffee that’ll keep your wits about you. So hurry up and add these cocktail recipes to your Turkey Day menu.

Here’s a whiskey sour that makes your fall-flavor dreams come true.

Add ingredients to a shaker and shake without ice. Pour into a glass and garnish with grated nutmeg and a dried apple slice.

This twist on the old-fashioned adds an autumnal flavor that will keep this classic feeling fresh.

Combine all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice. Stir until chilled and diluted. Strain into a rocks glass with a large cube. Garnish with an orange peel studded with cloves.

The delicious spice that goes into a pie doesn’t have to be just for lattes or baked goods.

Cover the rim of a stemless wineglass in simple syrup. Dip in cinnamon sugar and add ice to the glass. Pour in pumpkin-spice liqueur and Josh Cellars sauvignon blanc. Stir, then top off the glass with seltzer.

This three-ingredient cocktail is easy to whip up but will taste like it was complicated and time-consuming.

Mix cider and cinnamon whiskey in a Champagne flute. Top with Champagne, then stir lightly until incorporated. Garnish with an apple slice.

A sweet, fizzy sipper to enjoy before dinner.

Add all liquid ingredients to a stemless wineglass. Add ice. Stir to incorporate, then garnish.

A roasty, toasty espresso martini to enjoy after the big dinner.

Shake ingredients hard with ice until frothy, about 15 seconds. Double-strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass. Garnish with coffee beans, nutmeg, and cinnamon.

This sumptuous hot cocktail makes a great Thanksgiving treat.

In a mug, dissolve the sugar cubes in a little hot water. Add rum and butter. Fill the mug with hot water. Sprinkle nutmeg on top.

The margarita isn’t just a summer drink anymore.

In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients with ice and shake. Rim a glass with cinnamon sugar and serve over rocks. Garnish with slices of lime and orange.

You need to keep the booze flowing to keep the mood light and the conversation going. So mix together this sangria recipe that’ll satiate any apple-cider lover.

Place apples, orange, and cloves in a large pitcher. Drizzle honey over the fruit, then add in apple cider, rum, ginger beer, and white wine. Stir to mix. Top with ice and let chill for 20 minutes before serving. Serve in glasses, including the chunks of fruit.

Whoever invented pouring bourbon into a cup of tea, we want to give you a big hug.

Boil water in a teapot. Steep star anise pod or tea bag inside. Add bourbon, honey, lemon, and Tiki bitters to a mug. Stir. Serve in glass mugs with a spoon and the teapot. To enjoy, pour tea over cocktail base to taste and stir.

This aperitivo is the perfect refreshment before you start serving those heavy Thanksgiving dishes.

Pour Campari and sweet vermouth into a highball glass filled with ice. Top with club soda. Garnish with an orange twist.

A balanced spin on the Manhattan that uses Scotch whisky, this cocktail will impress any fan of brown liquor.

Stir the Scotch, vermouth, and bitters well with cracked ice. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Garnish with a lemon twist.

Simple enough to whip up in under five minutes, this cocktail has enough Scotch to knock Grandpa under the table.

Stir the Scotch and amaretto well with cracked ice in a mixing glass. Strain over fresh ice into an old-fashioned glass.

If you’re a big fan of cranberry sauce (the one that comes in a can), you can cure your cranberry craving with this vodka cocktail.

Shake ingredients in a shaker with cracked ice. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, then garnish with lime.

This green-tinged cocktail tastes fresh and slightly tart, but it’s boozy enough to chill you out after that heavy holiday meal.

Add all ingredients into a shaker. Shake well with cracked ice. Strain into a coupe glass. Garnish with a lime wedge and Luxardo cherries.

The Black Russian is the espresso martini’s cooler, more laid-back cousin. It’s so simple to make and yet deliciously complex in taste.

Stir ingredients with ice in a mixing glass. Strain into an old-fashioned glass over fresh ice.

Sometimes you don’t want to have to choose between two options, because you want to have it all! And you can have it both ways, with this gin-and-vodka martini, the vesper.

Stir ingredients briskly with ice in a mixing tin until very cold. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Garnish with a large, thin-cut lemon peel.

Why not turn your holiday gathering into an international experience? Incorporate this Russian classic into your cocktail rotation.

Squeeze lime juice into a copper mug (or a Collins glass) and drop in the spent hull. Add ice cubes, then pour in the vodka and fill with cold ginger beer. Serve with a stirring rod.

This rum cocktail will bring back fond memories of warmer weather.

Fill a tall glass with ice cubes. Add rum. Pour in ginger beer and lime juice. Stir with a barspoon, then garnish with a lime wedge.

Holidays are synonymous with Champagne, so pop open a bottle of bubbly and pour out one of these delicious cocktails.

Stir rum, lime juice, and honey thoroughly with cracked ice in a chilled cocktail shaker. Pour unstrained into a Collins glass. Top with Champagne.

During her three-day tour of India, the Princess of Wales attended the 2026 Earthshot Prize Ceremony in Mumbai. Prince William founded the initiative in 2020, and it awards environmental solutions with grants to scale and advance their projects.

For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

An elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

"I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. Slightly root stretch when you come to the top of the head instead of curling too close to the scalp."

To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

#6701. Couples Need to Stop Being So Weird About GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto VI came out last Thursday, and somehow the most unbearable thing about it isn't the grown men playing the game—it's the couples.

After the release of the game, my feed became a nonstop slideshow of printed contracts, handmade gift baskets, and girlfriends narrating their boyfriends' disappearance into Vice City like it's a deployment. Couples posted printed agreements that grant the player 10 full days of uninterrupted access.

I'm not here to tell anyone not to play a video game. People should do what makes them happy. But why are we all being so weird about a video game?

Ten days off from the relationship, so a man can play a game. I'd like to meet the woman who has ever been granted a 10-day leave from her partner, her family, her job, and the emotional labor of every relationship in her life. Women don't get to just disappear to pursue their hobbies.

Some women in relationships are putting together “offerings” for their partner. One viral example involved a GTA-themed gift basket stocked with snacks and drinks for the player's sessions. Another woman posted a Target-run basket of her boyfriend's favorite snacks with the caption, "This is your sign to make your man a GTA 6 basket!"

No. It's not. When was the last time he made you a basket for one of your hobbies?

On the flip side, some men are gifting their partners a basket, with the idea that women need something in return—a little distraction to keep busy while he's busy. Women are not toddlers who need to be handed a snack and a coloring book while the grown-ups play. We have friends. We have jobs. We have entire lives that existed before his Rockstar account and will exist after it. We'll be fine. We might even enjoy the quiet!

It all begs the question: Why can't men just have hobbies like normal people? Women have hobbies all the time. We go to pilates, we read, we get absorbed in a show, and nobody drafts a legal document. Let’s keep up that energy. Just play the game and also make time for the rest of your life!

But it isn’t just about people finding the time to play the game. There’s separate discourse among couples about the relationship players maintain with Lucia, the main female character.

Online, some women have expressed feeling jealous of Lucia. Around the game's lead-up, users on TikTok and Instagram were claiming that boyfriends who nurture a virtual relationship with Lucia could be considered cheating. A YouGov poll of 4,000 adults found around 6 percent would consider dating in games like GTA VI to be infidelity. That's a generally small number, but it's still making headway on social media.

Lucia is a character. She is pixels. If your relationship can be undone by a woman who exists only to rob a gas station with your boyfriend, the problem was never Lucia.

To be fair, some women have leaned into the joke. One girlfriend gifted her boyfriend the game with a four-rule counter-contract that ended with the line "Lucia is not your real girlfriend." I respect the bit—but it still icks me out.

On the other hand, there have been people claiming that GTA 6 is teaching men to be better partners. I’d like to politely disagree. The theory goes that watching Jason treat Lucia well, and putting effort into that relationship on screen, will make players better boyfriends in real life.

I'm glad they're being attentive to Lucia. I mean that. It’s a nice change to see the video game encouraging men to be decent human beings (though the bar is low). But at the end of the day, they're buying flowers, fixing things up, and doing the emotional work for a woman who doesn't exist, while their actual girlfriends are across the room eating a basket of Swedish Fish.

Can we all get real for a second? What grown man needs a video game to teach him how to treat a partner? Showing up, communicating, and putting in effort are not secret skills only unlocked by a video game. I promise you your boyfriend is not learning valuable relationship skills playing GTA 6.

So to any couples out there being particularly weird about GTA 6: play the game, enjoy it, and please just be normal. Be a person with a hobby. It really isn't that deep.

This is the dream stocking stuffer for your friend who likes to hike. It’s small enough to tuck in their backpack, but powerful enough to replace binoculars and telescopes. They’ll love birdwatching with this.

#6699. The 15 Most Thoughtful Personalized Gifts

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

These will make shopping easier than ever this year.

It might only be November, but the holidays are just around the corner, and with Hanukkah starting early this year on December 4, I’m already collecting gifts for everyone I love. Getting ahead of the curve has its perks: fewer frantic shipping fees, for one, and enough time to find something that feels genuinely special.

The easiest way to make a gift special? Get it personalized. Because who wants to tear through wrapping paper only to find the same thing everyone else is getting this season? Go the custom route, and even a classic gift feels like it was made just for them (because, well, it was).

Think engraved ID bracelets and signet rings for the guys, birthstone bracelets and sparkly initial pendants for the women in your life, and personalized sports merch for the fan whose team is a whole personality trait. Add sentimental photo albums full of family memories and a few delightfully quirky surprises they’ll never see coming, and you’ve got a list worth getting a head start on. Here are some of our favorite personalized gift ideas for the holidays this year.

Know someone who takes great pleasure in writing hand-written letters? Make their next correspondence even more exciting with personalized writing paper from Smythson. Customize everything from the size and color of the paper, the text and motif at the top of the paper, and the tissue lining and border on the envelopes.

Engraved jewelry is one of the classiest personalized gifts you can get for someone, especially when it’s simple and refined like this ID chain bracelet from Miansai. I got this bracelet for my boyfriend with his name engraved on it for the holidays last year, and he wears it pretty much every day.

A personalized jersey is a no-brainer for anyone with a favorite sports team. The Fanatics custom shop has merch for NFL, MLB, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLS, and even college teams, so it really has something for every kind of sports fan. And it’s not just jerseys—there’s also custom drinkware, bags, accessories, and more.

Even if your giftee isn’t super into astrology, they’ll appreciate a candle that’s just for them (or, well, anyone that shares their birthday). If they are into astrology, they’ll love all the fun facts about their birthday on the candle’s label, including their Zodiac sign, element, constellation, tarot card, and more. And all you have to know is their birthday, so it’s a pretty easy gift.

Speaking of birthdays, birthstone jewelry is another classic gift that’s personalized by design. And all you have to know is their birth month to get it right. Brilliant Earth has a great selection of birthstone jewelry, from pendant necklaces and colorful earrings to gemstone tennis bracelets and rings. You can even add multiple birthstones to this eternity lab diamond ring, so you can personalize it with the birthstones of everyone in your family.

For the one who spends their weekends on the golf course: They’ll truly impress their golf buddies with a box of personalized golf balls. And it comes with tees, a divot tool, and poker-chip ball markers so they have everything they need.

If you have the time and want to do something really special, order one of these luxury lighters from S.T. Dupont and get it engraved in person at a local engraving shop or jewelry repair store. The extra effort will show, and your giftee will have something to carry with them wherever they go for years to come.

You’ll have fun playing around with all the features in Ralph Lauren’s online custom hat maker—we certainly have. Choose the color and add a name, logo, or monogram, and the result will be a one-of-a-kind baseball cap your giftee will wear all the time.

Don’t just print out a photo and call it a day; get it printed on glass for something truly unique. Upload your photo to Fracture and personalize it even more with colorful borders, templates, frames, and stands.

Ever gone into a comic book store and seen the walls of Funko POP action figures from every franchise you can imagine? Having cute action figures of all your favorite Star Wars characters is great, but imagine how cool it would be to give someone an action figure of themself. With Funko POP, you can do just that—and you’ll have fun building it. You can even get a pair of Funko POP figures, so you can include yourself in it, too.

If you’re looking for a romantic personalized gift for your partner, surprise them with a watercolor painting of the place where you had your first date or the spot where you got engaged. Whether it was a local coffee shop, beloved movie theater, or beautiful outdoor space, it’ll look good painted above your names.

In a world where everything is online and in the cloud, a physical photo album is all the more sentimental and special. Artifact Uprising makes putting together a photo album easy, and the result is high quality and beautiful. It’s something they’ll want to display on their coffee table for everyone to see.

Gifts based on birthdays is a common theme in this gift guide, but what can we say? It’s an easy way to personalize stuff. If they’re a history buff (or just love reading the news), they’ll enjoy flipping through this customized book of newspaper headlines from their birthday through the years.

You know that person who is absolutely obsessed with their dog or cat? (Okay, it’s me.) They’ll obsess over any gift that has to do with their beloved pet, like this custom sweatshirt embroidered with the face of their dog or cat. Just upload a photo of their pet (you can probably find one on their Facebook or Instagram) and choose a sweater color and size.

A customized L.L. Bean tote bag is something they’ll use all the time. It’s one of our favorite gifts of all time, and it’s an absolute classic.

#6698. Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour Is Getting a Concert Film and Documentary

Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour may have wrapped in September, but fans will soon get another chance to experience it. Following an initial teaser on November 23, the singer announced on November 24 that both a concert film and a documentary for the tour are set to premiere on Peacock.

The news comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.

Here’s everything we know about the projects so far.

The documentary—titled The Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour —follows Grande “during the 30 days leading up to the opening of her sold-out tour as she and her team race to bring the ambitious production to life,” according to Peacock. “At the same time, Grande is putting the finishing touches on her eighth studio album, giving audiences an intimate window into her creative process during a pivotal moment.”

The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film “journeys through the collapse of her reality, a cosmic rebirth, a reconnection with her inner child, and the memories that shaped her. She transforms the Eternal Sunshine Tour into a cinematic celebration of healing, connection, and the music that has defined her life.”

Her Eternal Sunshine Tour began in Oakland, California, on June 6 and concluded on September 1 following 10 performances at London’s O2 Arena. The shows featured music from across her discography, including Eternal Sunshine, Positions, and her latest album, Petal, which was released in July.

The tour also marked Grande’s return to the concert stage following her 2019 Sweetener World Tour. Throughout the run, she performed in custom looks from designers including Alexander McQueen, Givenchy, and Vivienne Westwood, styled by Law Roach.

Grande shared the first teaser on Instagram on November 23, in collaboration with Peacock and Team Ariana.

The video features footage of Grande performing the title track from Eternal Sunshine. As the performance ends, the screen reveals the message: “Coming soon to… Peacock.”

During an August interview with Vosk in the City, Grande reflected on how her latest tour differed from her previous experiences performing live.

“I think my last tour I wasn’t necessarily in the same place in life, and I wasn’t able to be as present as I am this time,” she explained, describing the Eternal Sunshine Tour as “such a beautiful corrective experience.”

Grande also spoke about reconnecting with longtime fans through songs spanning more than a decade of her career.

In August, her representative confirmed that the singer planned to step away from public-facing work following the tour. Grande later addressed the decision during a concert in Chicago, explaining that it had been made well in advance.

“It is something that I have decided; it’s a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago, and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the audience.

The Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour documentary premieres on Peacock on December 11. The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film arrives on December 12.

#6696. Why Do We All Love a Small-Town Holiday Romance? Guarding Stars Might Have the Answer

The fantasy of falling in love in a small town has surprisingly little to do with the small town itself.

I’ll find any excuse to cozy up with a holiday rom-com, so when Guarding Stars dropped on Netflix, it was a no-brainer. Gossip Girl and Supernatural alumni Leighton Meester and Jared Padalecki are embracing one of my favorite tropes: the good old “small-town holiday romance.” Leighton’s character Hannah goes with Jared’s character Jack to his hometown pretending to be his girlfriend, while actually serving as his bodyguard. It got me thinking: Whether we’re die-hard city dwellers or seasoned travelers, why do we still love the home-for-the-holidays romance trope?

For me, the answer lies in how this specific genre taps into our own deep-rooted desire for escapism. We’ve seen these kinds of fake girlfriend or friends-to-lovers storylines play out a million times before, so their predictability is incredibly comforting to watch. We have, quite literally, seen this film before. And during the heightened chaos of the holiday season, it places viewers in the safe bubble many people crave.

Plus, the small-town setting in Guarding Stars is perfectly cozy. The two head to Jack’s obnoxiously large family home in Montana that’s been pristinely decorated in Nancy Meyers–inspired aesthetics. And much like in one of my favorite holiday movies, The Family Stone, the house itself is just part of the fantasy. The idea of being welcomed into a close-knit community with acceptance might be exactly what we dream of the holidays being like. Being loved by a family that, in the case of Hannah, is not even your own is really intoxicating.

Even the dating looks more fun. Hannah and Jack spend the whole movie dating their way around town, doing cutesy romantic things like attending the local rodeo, getting caught on a kiss cam, and mucking out horses together in the family stables. These wouldn’t be your go-to date locations in a more urban, city-based setting, so their dating experience feels playful and different from everyday life.

And Guarding Stars finds a way to elevate this trope. Hannah isn’t actively looking for a man when all of this unfolds. She’s just doing her job as a bodyguard when she inadvertently falls into a snowball of festive shenanigans. Hannah is doing fine on her own, but there’s something sweet about watching her let her guard down. Guarding Stars gently suggests that by Hannah making herself a little more vulnerable, she’s making room for more people to love and support her. As someone who tends to handle the hard stuff alone (eldest daughter syndrome, anyone?), that really resonated with me.

So often, this genre leans toward women going to the small town and being “fixed” or changed by the relationship they encounter. Their lives in the big city are unsatisfying, actually, and they really would rather work at the Christmas tree farm. That doesn’t happen here. She ends up back in New York City, and that’s where the final action set piece of the movie happens.

Guarding Stars shows that the small-town holiday romance trope can change and evolve without losing its festive magic, because it’s about comfort and connection. We can be cozy and keep our apartments in New York City, and I’m thankful for that this holiday season.

#6694. Before & After: Dark, Underutilized Storage Spaces Make Way for a Cozy Library, Breakfast Nook, and Family Room

An intentional gut renovation turned dead space into room for a growing family.

With certain homes, it can take time (and a designer’s eye) to realize the full potential. For some, that means living within a less-than-perfect layout for a while to really understand the pain points. When a couple with twin boys bought this Greek Revival farmhouse in Connecticut’s tony Fairfield County in 2022, they knew changes were in store down the line.

“It didn’t feel like them yet,” says the project’s interior designer, Vivian Shao Chen. “The house was in great condition, but the layout didn’t work for how they lived.” The 1940s home had a considerable amount of dead space, including entire rooms and shadowy corners that felt disconnected from the rest of the home.

On top of that, planning a rework around the two youngsters was an additional challenge. “The question was always how a space can grow with them: what deserves the investment and what should stay flexible,” Chen adds.

Once Chen began working on the project in 2024, she refocused the homeowners' attention away from the idea of a home addition and sparse, “Scandinavian beach house” aesthetic toward a warmer, more traditional sensibility in line with the house’s original period style.

“I always start with trying to understand existing site conditions as much as possible,” Chen says. “What is the architectural language of the house? Where is it inconsistent, what can we edit? Often, very small but thoughtful changes can make all the difference.”

Ultimately, a gut renovation was necessary to address the home’s layout limitations, and new millwork was added throughout to provide character and a strong visual throughline. Now, each space has its own unique identity and every corner is packed with purpose—with plenty of wiggle room to allow for the young family’s necessary changes over time.

“This house feels so warm, cozy, and grounding,” Chen says. “Our hope is that we've designed for their current season of life and set a good foundation for the future without overdesigning, leaving room for the house to change as life does.”

FAST FACTSDesigner: Vivian Shao ChenContractor: The O'Dell GroupStylist: Andrew Carter ThomasLocation: Weston, CTThe Space: A three-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bath home across 4,218 square feet

A formerly nondescript pass-through area, the home’s entry now gives visitors a proper greeting with its lush Sandberg wallpaper bridging indoors and out. “It speaks to the beautiful Connecticut setting we are in and also says, ‘Welcome, come in and relax, it’s not too formal here,’” notes Chen.

Additionally, choosing darker tones in a foyer or hallway is a great way to emphasize an airier mood elsewhere. “These transition spaces are meant to feel cozy, enveloping and a little moody, so when you step into the open expanse of the living room, with all its light and views, the house seems to exhale,” the designer adds.

One space that was spared a major redesign was the living room, as its existing architecture already suited the household’s needs. “The living room has always been a breath of fresh air in the house, being the first big expanse you walk into, with wonderful views out onto the property and beautiful daylight,” Chen attests.

A touch-up was still in order, though. Chen refreshed the wall color and chose updated furnishings upholstered in velvet and linen to complement the family’s antique Chinese chest, which became the natural focal point in the room. “The contrasting elements balance out the lightness of the room in a way that feels quiet and grounding,” she adds.

One of the biggest triumphs of a home renovation is when an awkward spare room becomes the new go-to gathering spot—and that’s exactly what happened with this former storage space-turned-library.

Chen removed an en suite powder room, which helped anchor the layout around a seating area instead of feeling transitory. She then wrapped the room in quarter-sawn white oak millwork, which layered in all the stately personality that the former space was missing.

The millwork, while providing shelving and storage opportunities, also included a media center, a built-in desk, and a daybed. “The daybed cushions are intentionally sized like twin mattresses, so with a fitted sheet they become an extra bed for guests or sleepovers,” Chen says.

The space is now appropriately flexible, able to be cordoned off from the main living room with pocket doors or inviting enough for games or movies, with classic library sconces that make it especially cozy at night.

“The kitchen was a gut renovation, but in reviewing the layout, I felt like the bones were mostly right,” Chen muses. “It just needed a lot of editing and new finishes.” Without altering the footprint, Chen maximized the flow of the space by removing the ceiling beams, relocating the refrigerator, scaling up the windows overlooking the yard, and adding interior windows to open up views to the adjacent mudroom and breakfast room.

Then there was the kitchen island: a solid white oak piece on custom turned legs, topped with a seamless Calacatta Monet slab that Chen calls “sublime.” Overhead, an artful single pendant by Roll & Hill adds a far more impactful ambiance than a trio ever could. “It’s about finding restraint and negative space where it can make an impact,” Chen notes.

One notable omission in the cook space is the presence of upper cabinets—Chen chose hutch cabinets instead that “hide a microwave, a pantry, and a coffee station.” Apart from the millwork, finishes, and fixtures, the kitchen also includes all-new appliances, aside from the statement-making blue La Cornue range that was already in the home.

Even if breakfasting outdoors is only realistic for a few months in the Northeast, this nook right off the kitchen now provides the illusion of alfresco enjoyment. Originally, the room felt too out of step with the rest of the home, and even its most desirable feature—the view out of the picture window—was hard to appreciate in such a segmented space.

Chen reimagined the room as an interior porch, replacing the entry wall with a muntin division to lure guests from the kitchen to this sunny spot. The nook’s newly added bay windows provide more light and dimension, and its nickel-gap paneling has a soft, rustic touch. Chen also tucked a built-in banquette into the bay for the most obvious purpose: “You're now sitting in the view, not just looking at it.”

Through the breakfast room (and another set of muntin dividers) is the cozy, cocooning dining room. Rather than flooding this windowless room with light, Chen employed a clever strategy to maximize the ambiance. “The custom plaster finish on the walls and ceiling has a subtle sheen that catches the light, so what was once the room's drawback is now its greatest charm,” she notes.

Basements without a proper design outlook are destined to become clutter overflow areas. That’s exactly what was happening on the home’s lower level, so a gut renovation was in order.

To make the space more livable, Chen added millwork to conceal laundry and utility access, plush furnishings, and a new door and windows that open up to a walk-out terrace. Though the low ceiling had to stay, new nickel-gap paneling makes the space feel cozy rather than cramped. “The room reads as a true family room,” she says.

The former mudroom was a rough-and-tumble catch-all passage, but considering that this area functions as the family’s main entrance, it deserved a gut renovation that they could take pride in—starting with the floor. Chen swapped out the no-nonsense tile for a striking limestone checkerboard. “The light squares are actually the same limestone as the kitchen floor, only done in a different pattern,” she says.

New lockers and coat cabinets along the perimeter conceal all the out-the-door essentials, while a floating console, clad in drab olive, has the look of an antique find but was custom-made for the space. It functions as the necessary landing zone that every bustling family home needs; Chen intentionally kept the bottom open for sliding packages and storage baskets (and perhaps the odd shoe) out of the way.

This office bathroom was previously awash in neutrals but still managed to look dark and drab, so Chen revitalized it with a much-needed dose of drama. Her go-to design reference? Old New York members’ clubs.

“Instead of wrapping the room in dark wood, we kept the stained wood to the custom vanity and let color and pattern do the rest,” she notes. Outfitted with the white penny-tile floor, striped zellige in the shower, and racing-green color drenching, the space now nods to tradition while keeping it playful.

“The primary bedroom already had so much going for it: beautiful windows, generous proportions, and absolutely peaceful,” Chen attests. “Our goal was to keep and elevate those qualities.”

Chen amplified the room’s natural daylight with a fresh coat of Farrow & Ball's Slipper Satin, then softened the space with more natural textures, including a slipcovered linen bed, woven linen for the drapery, and a textured wool rug. Even though the bedroom has one of the most restrained palettes in the whole home, it celebrates textural variation.

To maintain the same serene but texturally rich feel as the adjoining primary bedroom, the bathroom needed a layout and material rework. To make the most of a modest footprint, Chen opted for slim Shaker linen cabinets and a floating vanity. “Seeing the floor continue beneath it tricks the eye, making the room feel larger than its actual standing space,” she says.

The room’s warm marble floors and soft off-white color also provide an ideal backdrop for the room’s showstopper moment: a Calacatta Viola slab shower and backsplash, with deep, wine-toned veining.

For now, the twin boys share this bedroom, so the existing architecture was left alone. Instead, the focus was on enriching the palette with taupe, cream, blue, and copper tones and choosing furnishings that can flex over time. “The art is by the boys themselves, which was so special to incorporate into the room,” says Chen.

Vivian Shao Chen is an interior designer specializing in whole-home designs, including interior architecture. She has over 15 years of architectural training and professional experience, and focuses on residential interiors and lifestyle design, including home goods and clothing.

#6692. “Two Girls Who Speak All the Time About Politics”: Tao Okamoto and Virginie Efira Take On Capitalism in All of a Sudden

Okamoto and Efira shared the Best Actress Award at Cannes, where All of a Sudden premiered this summer

We’re all seeking comfort as the world ends. Environmental, economic, and political pressures weigh heavily on our minds as tangible solutions feel farther and farther out of reach. Solace is a rare commodity in a world controlled by unrelenting capitalist forces. In All of a Sudden, filmmaker Ryusuke Hamaguchi suggests that as we face tragedy, we must remember our vital need for human connection.

All of a Sudden tells the story of two women who forge a formidable friendship as they face personal and professional hardship. Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira) runs an elder-care facility near Paris, where she introduces a “Humanitude” methodology designed to treat patients with dignity and introduce listening-heavy caretaking practice. She befriends Mari (Tao Okamoto), a terminally ill theater director from Japan. Ryusuke chronicles this relationship through extended, emotional conversations, spoken in both Japanese and French, and covering topics from identity to mortality.

The film is an adaptation of a nonfiction book, When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist, which collects correspondence from two Japanese-speaking academics as they reflect on health care and death during the last few months of philosopher Makiko Miyano’s life (who inspired Okamoto’s character). Instead of keeping the fact that the two pen pals spoke the same language, he introduced French and moved the story to Paris. This small change forced the story to confront language gaps, exploring the power of conversation and listening and asserting that so much can be achieved through this mediation.

Efira and Okamoto understand their characters’ simmering anxieties and outlooks on the world, providing the bedrock for these impressively naturalistic performances. The two actresses sustain long, philosophical conversation with such intensity throughout the entire three hours and 16 minutes. In a rare occurrence, the two shared the Best Actress Award at the Cannes Film Festival, where the movie premiered this summer. In the film, their budding friendship serves as a sounding board for each other, as Marie-Lou grapples with the pressure of capitalism on her medical staff and Mari comes to terms with the end of her life. In typical fashion, Ryusuke lets the camera linger on these two actresses during these prolonged philosophical interactions, forcing the audience to sit with the gravity of their situations.

Ahead of the theatrical release of Ryusuke’s latest feature film, Bazaar spoke to Efira and Okamoto about the first time they read the script, how they built an intimate bond despite speaking two different languages, and the punk, anti-capitalist edge fueling this intimate, conversation-heavy film.

Tao Okamoto: It’s the scene where she talks about capitalism while writing on the whiteboard. That’s one of the strangest scenes in the movie. I felt connected to the character because I am also a climate activist myself. I’ve been spreading the word about climate crises on podcasts, and I talk about it daily. When I read the part, I felt, “I need to play this character.”

Virginie Efira: It’s the same for me, because this scene is so special. When I read it, the movie felt like one of the most profound, special, and radical readings. You have two girls who speak all the time about politics. We don’t see that. I never see that in other movies. Sometimes, when a director wants to put something philosophical, political, or intellectual, they say, “Maybe we’ll do three minutes,” otherwise the audience will be bored. No, this movie spent 15 minutes [discussing capitalism], and I said, “Oh yes, that’s so punk!” The film has its own language. When I read All of a Sudden, I could hear the language of the movie, and I wanted to approach it. When I met Tao, I thought, “Oh, we are so lucky to be an actress and work with [Ryusuke], but also to share this material with him.”

VE: I only knew one word in Japanese before making the movie. Then, to be able to speak Japanese at a high level, because the character studied in Japan, I must first learn to read, then learn to embody the language. Finding the language of the movie was strange. There’s a flat and natural way to play [in one of Ryusuke’s movies]. He spoke to me about Cassavetes and Gena Rowlands, but also about Bresson. Neutral performances. You find it when you open up, and when I opened to Tao, we discovered the right language for the movie. We did a lot of flat readings before shooting. We never rehearsed in motion, so when we finally performed for the first time, we awakened the text.

TO: I’m going to add that because I started my career in America, finding a middle ground by using a language that’s not my mother tongue is normal for me. On the surface, that part wasn’t a challenge for me. Finding the language for this film and respecting Hamaguchi’s way of working were priorities. We were naturally drawn to his talent and wanted to make his dream happen and be part of it.

TO: I joined this project way after Virginie. I luckily had months to prepare with him, and during rehearsals, you drop all emotion and read the text as if you were reading numbers. On top of that, I got to visit some institutes, such as the Cancer Research Center and places where people work with disabled people, to build up my understanding of my role’s point of view. Reading the text over and over was a unique experience for me. [Ryusuke] can really listen to the actor’s voice and tell the difference between someone who is simply reading and someone really concentrating. Even though you’re not supposed to put any emotions, you have to be present; you have to be there. I’ve never experienced such rich, profound preparation for a role.

VE: We shot in a real nursing home. There was a mix between fiction and reality. Sometimes filmmaking becomes standardized, with no room left to breathe, but with Hamaguchi, you’re sure he will leave room for the unexpected and for uncertainty. It allows you to embrace the unpredictability of reality. He’s not looking for an accident, but for the ability to be in the present. A viewer of Hamaguchi’s work will always feel a sensation of documentation, but it’s still always cinema. To be an actor in his movies is to be naturalistic, to be in the present, to capture some details and really embrace this unpredictability. The filming process becomes an adventure he wants you to have. One day, he told me, “I hope that you will find the light.” He said a lot of cryptic things. He said to me, “Don’t use your text like a tool; just go inside the text.”

TO: The script is already amazing. And I could read it over and over again, and that was a joy. But he mentioned that I should read the original book. It’s about two women exchanging letters—or emails. They are real people who the characters are modeled after. I wanted to please the people who know these women, not to make them too different from them. I first put pressure on myself to portray this woman as close to the real person, but it was impossible for me because this person passed away in 2019. I couldn’t do much research, so I interviewed her mother and the co-writer. That provided me with a lot of clues, but reading their exchanged letters already gave me the soul of this movie.

VE: He gives the book to the actresses, but also to the entire team. I never felt something so collective, and you will feel it in the movie, from the sound engineer to someone who only stayed two days on set. I also met the anthropologist. When you read this book, it’s full of life. It gives you a perceptible beauty of things. The book has a kind of energy; it helps you keep a level of optimism even when you know the situation is hopeless. In this book, it speaks about what it’s like to be alive. Maybe there’s beauty in life because we are going to die.

TO: For me, I came on this project at the last minute, only a month before. Virginie was so dedicated to studying Japanese from scratch; it was so impressive how she studied all this writing, reading, and lines. Seeing that, I had a huge admiration, like “Who can do this!?” As you can see, Virginie’s so charming; nobody would hate her. It was so easy for me to be drawn to her as a person, as the characters in the movie were discovering each other.

VE: We got to know each other through the shoot. I was happy not to know much at the beginning and to progressively get deeper into our relationship. We lived all that together. I conflate Marie-Lou’s feelings for Mari with Virginie’s feelings for Tao, because we share that. It will be an end, not a tragic one like in the movie, but it will be an end. But I know Tao will carry this experience in her heart forever, and I will too. He let us feel what we want to feel.

TO: I study environmental issues, and I always thought capitalism is responsible for our world’s issues. Something I didn’t know until I read this script was that capitalism doesn’t only exploit our environment, but also our human bodies—human labor and our time. When I connected those dots, I realized all the problems could be blamed on capitalism. We’re looking for time and looking for happiness—or security—and all these things can be related to a capitalistic way of living. I think it’s great that Hamaguchi connected that fundamental issue to Marie-Lou’s situation in the elderly home. She’s frustrated, as is Marie. She’s battling her cancer, and it can be connected to this economic issue.

VE: Cinema can show bodies, fatigue, and with Marie-Lou, you see a certain fatigue because capitalism creates it. How do we deal with that? We say, “Oh, capitalism’s not good. We don’t have time. And we want to be richer and richer.” But how do we fight that, because everything is already there? I come from France, and you see all the young people outside. The real question is, what can cinema do with that? It’s not a theoretical thing, but Hamaguchi can find a solution. It’s speaking, listening to the other, sharing ideas; it’s movement. If I look for a solution to this problem with money, I’ll remain a prisoner of this way of functioning. Even if you think you’re not in a stage of capitalism, you are.

This interview has been condensed and edited for clarity.

#6691. A Case for Being Single During the Holidays

valentine’s Day is the official holiday for couples—so why does the fall and winter holiday season feel like a love and relationship fest?

This time of year has literally been deemed “cuffing season”: You’re encouraged to take couples pictures at a pumpkin patch, bring a date to Thanksgiving, drink hot cocoa by the fireplace at Christmas, and have someone special to kiss at midnight on New Year’s Eve.

But even though we’ve been inundated with countless signs that this is the best time to couple up, I’m going to go out on a limb here and say that I actually think there’s no better time than the holiday season to be single.

“The holidays can actually be a great time for creating our own traditions and sense of self,” relationship expert Bethany Nicole tells Cosmopolitan. “Being single over the holidays gives us a much-needed time of rest, reflection, and recalibration.”

So instead of falling victim to the pressures of coupling up during the holidays, why not just lean into being single instead? You might even find yourself enjoying the holidays more. Why? Thought you’d never ask:

According to Newsweek, 65 percent of Americans admitted that they’re stressed about the amount of money they’ll spend during the holidays. And for 73 percent of them, this financial stress actually makes the holidays less enjoyable. Can you guess who people are spending most of this money on? That’s right: their children and their romantic partners.

Sure, you might still have to get your parents, siblings, and your weird aunt a holiday gift—but isn’t it satisfying knowing that you don’t have to budget a huge chunk of change for yet another person in your life? By staying single during the holidays, you’re actually keeping your pockets happier.

The holidays are a time to spend with loved ones. But with so many events centered around the holidays, you might be spending more of that precious time with someone you’re just getting to know instead of with your friends and family. Assuming you like your friends and family, this is not the best ratio!

When you’re single, you can spend the holiday season with whoever you want. You can go to endless friendsgivings without having to drag along a plus-one, you can eat Thanksgiving dinner comfortably with your family without having to check on someone else, and it’s actually really fun to go out on New Year’s Eve with your best friends.

On the other side of the coin, family time in general is not for the weak. I get that, because mine isn’t either. If you were in a relationship, you’d probably be panicking right now about how to explain to your partner that your aunt is really funny if you ignore that she hates your mother or that your dad salutes the turkey before he cuts into it. But when you don’t have a date to Thanksgiving, you can just enjoy the weird and disturbing quirks of your family without having to explain them away to your partner.

When you’re coupled up, you’re expected to be “selfless” and “generous.” Ew. When you’re single, on the other hand, you can just be your normal, selfish self—and I truly think that’s beautiful.

Someone with a partner would probably be expected to give up the last piece of the pumpkin pie or be giving with an extra big piece of turkey. But because you aren’t in a relationship, you can have as much pie as you want—without pretending like you’re not picking up the speed while eating so your partner doesn’t get more bites than you.

Being around your own family for the holidays is torture enough—imagine if you then had to add a partner’s family to the mix? Not just that, but you’d most likely have to pretend to like them, too. And even get to know them!

Meeting an S.O.’s friends and family is a lot of pressure. Even though the holidays are a time of joy and celebration, they’re also super stressful. And you just don’t need the added stress of trying to impress your boyfriend’s dad, who doesn’t believe women should be in leadership positions.

Sure, having a partner around the holidays is nice—doing romantic things with someone you care deeply about can really add to the experience. But if you really want a partner, you have the rest of the new year to try and find someone.

For now, I say save your money, hang out with your friends, and do what the holidays were intended for: eating pie until you’re sick.

The new collection draws heavily from Sierra Designs’ ‘70s heyday, with reworked versions of an archival down jacket and vest serving as the stars of the show. Both are made from lightweight Japanese nylon and utilize a 600-fill-power, 80/20 blend of down and feathers for insulation. They’re complemented by a range of vintage-y tees, thermals, totes, and caps.

The overall vibe is easygoing and not too techy—exactly the sort of stuff you’ll want to wear in everyday life, not just on some windswept summit. Which is what makes it so damn good. There’s no shortage of high-performance winter gear out there, but much of it falls short on the style front. This is the sort of stuff that’ll do the job but won’t have you looking like you just finished a black-diamond run. Wear it with chinos and hiking boots or jeans and sneakers. To the coffee shop on a blustery morning or the park for a day out with the family. Or, yeah, even in the great outdoors. Just make sure to snag whatever you like soon, as Buck Mason’s collaborations have a nasty habit of selling out.

#6689. 12 Things You Should Toss From Your Kitchen ASAP Before Thanksgiving

Experts say a quick kitchen edit now can save holiday stress later.

It’ll soon be the most important day of the year in the kitchen, so give yourself the gift of space and freedom from clutter by doing a quick purge.

“Thanksgiving needs every inch of counter, fridge, and cabinet space you’ve got,” says Ann Lightfoot, cofounder of DDH Home Organizing & Move Management. “A short edit beforehand means you can find the baster when you need it, the leftovers have somewhere to go, and you aren’t digging past three broken whisks to reach a serving spoon.”

But don’t overdo it! “You don’t need a Pinterest-perfect pantry. You need room to work,” says Lightfoot. “A full organizing project can easily turn into a weekend of half-finished bins, and that’s the last thing anyone needs in November.”

Instead of tearing apart the entire kitchen, focus on the areas and items that will have the most impact. “We always say edit before you organize, and this is the editing part: take things out,” says Lightfoot. “Do one quick pass, ask whether each item earns its space, and let the rest go. Labels and matching containers can wait until January.”

Ahead, here’s what experts say to get rid of ASAP so your kitchen will be ready for cooking and entertaining at Thanksgiving.

“Spices lose their flavor over time, and stale cinnamon or a two-year-old jar of sage will make itself known in your pie and stuffing,” says Lightfoot. “Check the dates on baking soda, baking powder, and flour too. Toss what’s past its prime and make a shopping list while you’re at it.”

Glasses with scratches just don’t look great. “I'm all for mixing vintage and contemporary pieces, but damaged drinking glasses and dishes should go,” says Kerrie Kelly, NKBA, FASID, CEO and creative director of Kerrie Kelly Studio, and NKBA 2026 National Board Chair. “Holiday entertaining is a wonderful excuse to take inventory and make sure you have enough functional pieces for your guests.”

“Three napkins and a stack of faded plates won't set a beautiful table. Let them go and start fresh,” says Nikki Boyd, organizing expert, author of Beautifully Organized, and founder of At Home With Nikki.

It’s amazing how stuff gets pushed to the back of the fridge, never to be seen again. “Fridge space is prime real estate on Thanksgiving, between the turkey, the sides, and everything guests bring,” says Lightfoot. “Clear out the half-empty dressings, the jam from last summer, and anything you can’t identify.”

Be honest with yourself. “If it hasn't come out for a single holiday in years, it's not waiting for this one,” says Boyd. “Keep heirlooms with stories, and release the rest.”

“Kitchen drawers have a way of collecting multiples of things we rarely need more than one of,” says Laura Kinsella, founder of Urban OrgaNYze. “Pull out your spatulas, peelers, measuring cups, and all those cooking tools that always seem to get stuck in the drawer. If you're not reaching for them when you're hosting 20 people, chances are you don't need them for a regular weeknight dinner either.”

“Your table is your stage. Burnt down candles and stained runners don't belong on it,” says Boyd.

Containers that have no lids need to go away ASAP. Ditto for lids that don’t have a container. “Before the holiday leftovers start piling up, take 10 minutes to match your food storage containers with their lids. Get rid of anything that's cracked, warped, or missing its match,” says Kinsella. “There's nothing more frustrating than having a refrigerator full of leftovers and realizing you can't find a single lid that fits!”

That bread maker you haven’t touched lately? The air fryer that’s collecting dust? It’s time to donate them. “Any big kitchenware item that you haven’t used for the past two to three holiday seasons needs to go,” says Amelia Meena, owner of Appleshine, Organization + Design.

If they’re in bad shape, treat yourself to some new ones. “Nonstick pans with a flaking coating and sheet pans warped beyond saving make cooking harder than it has to be,” says Lightfoot. “If you’ve been meaning to replace one, do it now so you aren’t stuck mid-recipe.”

Soy sauce and ketchup packets, plastic forks, extra napkins, and the stack of menus add up quickly. You’ll want that drawer space for foil, twine, and the meat thermometer, so toss the whole lot into the garbage immediately, says Lightfoot.

Stained, threadbare towels and thin pot holders aren’t safe for pulling a hot roasting pan out of the oven—plus, raggedy mitts don’t exactly scream “festive.” Pitch thin pot holders and recycle old towels into cleaning rags, then treat yourself to a cute new set of kitchen linens, says Lightfoot.

#6688. Jennifer Lawrence Sets the Record Straight on Those Blepharoplasty Rumors

The actress credits her makeup artist, Shayna Gold, as the mastermind behind her “bleph”

In this day and age, it’s almost a rite of passage for a celebrity to have plastic surgery rumors about them swirling online, but Jennifer Lawrence has been speaking her truth on the matter as of late.

Last week on Watch What Happens Live, the Hunger Games actress casually slipped into her conversation with host Andy Cohen that she has new breast implants and even credited her plastic surgeon, Steven Teitelbaum, for the “full C” cups.

She continues to set the record straight on her cosmetic procedures—this time shutting down rumors that she had a blepharoplasty. Online rumors quickly speculated that Lawrence had undergone upper eyelid surgery, but her latest Instagram post shuts them down. Her makeup artist, Shayna Gold, shared a mailer of products from the actress’s new haircare line, Mes, and Lawrence reposted the photo to her own story with a cheeky caption. “Iykyk she’s the one who did my bleph,” Lawrence wrote, crediting Gold and pointing to makeup as the reason she looks so wide awake, officially poking holes in any eyelid surgery rumors.

Lawrence has previously been open about her plastic surgery. In October, after gracing the cover of The Cut, she revealed she had work done following the birth of her second child, which the publication then specified as a boob job. One year earlier, the actress told The New Yorker, “Everything bounced back, pretty much, after the first one. Second one, nothing bounced back.”

While fans aren’t exactly sold on Lawrence’s denial of a bleph, makeup artists often do have tricks up their sleeves for faking an eyelid lift. For starters, placement matters. When emphasizing the crease, apply shadow above the natural crease. “I like patting shadows onto the lid first, then blending the edges after. Too much back-and-forth blending can make the shape disappear,” celebrity makeup artist Christian Briceno previously told Bazaar. Also, opt for an elongated look, like a soft wing, to make the eye look instantly bigger. This also applies to mascara—artists recommend focusing application on the outer corners versus the center.

#6687. The Secrets Behind Brittany Snow’s Press-Tour Glow

The actress is embracing a more intentional beauty routine with a little help from RéVive Skincare.

Though her recent red-carpet looks may beg to differ, Brittany Snow is no longer chasing perfection—at least when it comes to her appearance. Instead, the actress, who turned 40 this year and is starring in one of the moment’s most deliciously bingeable series, now in its second season, is focused on aging well and nourishing her skin with intention. “There’s something really freeing about realizing you don’t need to look perfect to feel confident,” Snow says. “I spent so much of my younger years unfortunately being aware of how I looked. Snow credits her makeup artist Charlie Riddle with introducing her to the luxe skin care brand and helping her evolve her relationship to beauty. “He has always focused on making my skin look like skin—healthy, hydrated, and luminous,” she says. “He understands that the better you take care of your skin, the less you need to cover it up.”

Throughout the current press tour, Riddle has been prepping Snow’s skin with RéVive; the brand has quickly become a staple in her personal routine, too. “I was initially drawn to how beautiful my skin felt when Charlie used the products on me,” she says. “There was this sense of hydration without feeling like I had a million things sitting on my face. In addition to the products’ elegant feel and innovative, science-based formulas, Snow also appreciates RéVive’s brand story. “RéVive was founded by a plastic surgeon whose research began with helping burn victims heal,” she says. “There’s something really meaningful to me about a beauty brand that was born out of wanting to help people.”

The complementary formulas work to renew skin overnight to reveal a healthier-looking, more radiant, and glowing complexion by morning.

“My skin goes through so much between filming, travel, and wearing makeup for hours,” she says. “By the end of the day, I really want something that feels rich and helps my skin look refreshed. After using them, my skin feels like glass.”

Glowing from the inside out, her recent appearances—be they in character on our TV screens or in late-night talk show clips on our phones—are proof both of RéVive’s results and the confidence that comes from feeling good in one’s own skin.

Tap into their current hyperfixation with one of SHEGLAM’s holiday collections.

#6684. What’s Trending in Holiday Decor This Year, According to Designers
